title: Information theory, entropy & compression
summary: Connect uncertainty, prediction loss, coding, and the limits of what a benchmark tells you.
html:
Connect uncertainty, prediction loss, coding, and the limits of what a benchmark tells you.

How the pieces connect

Define distribution → Score predictions → Compress → Interpret. Each transition is a place where an assumption can be inspected before the next layer of the system compounds it.

Surprise and entropy

The information content of an outcome with probability p is −log p. Rare outcomes carry more surprise. Entropy averages surprise under a distribution. With base-two logarithms the unit is bits; natural logarithms give nats. Entropy depends on what is being modeled and conditioned on.

Cross-entropy scores a predictor

Cross-entropy averages −log q(x) when outcomes are drawn from p but predicted using q. It equals entropy of p plus KL divergence from p to q where defined. Minimizing it rewards probability on observed outcomes, but a model can still assign high likelihood to harmful or factually false text if it appears in data.

Compression and language modeling

A better probability model can encode predictable symbols more efficiently. Language model perplexity is the exponential of average negative log likelihood in nats. Comparing perplexity across tokenizers or datasets without controlling their definitions is misleading because the prediction units differ.

Mutual information and representations

Mutual information measures dependence between variables: how much knowing one reduces uncertainty about another. A compressed representation is useful if it retains information needed for the downstream task. Compression alone does not guarantee meaningful, causal, or fair features.

Worked example

A fair coin has entropy 1 bit. A coin that always lands heads has entropy 0. A predictor assigning 0.9 to an event that occurs receives −ln(0.9)≈0.105 nats of loss; assigning 0.01 receives about 4.605 nats.

What goes wrong

Entropy of a model’s output distribution measures its uncertainty under its own beliefs. An confidently wrong model can have very low entropy.

Check your understanding

If token loss is 2 nats, what is perplexity?

Reveal the explanation

e²≈7.39. Interpret it only with the same tokenization, dataset, and loss accounting.

An operating model for information theory, entropy & compression

Information measures uncertainty under a distribution, not intelligence or factuality. Cross-entropy teaches a predictor to place probability mass on observed data. It does not directly optimize factual grounding, causal reasoning, safety, or a downstream task unless those are represented in data and the objective.

The gotcha. A clean workflow diagram describes dependency order. It does not prove that any boundary is correct; each transition needs its own observable acceptance test.

Worked system: lower cross-entropy, wrong comparison

Two language-model evaluations report losses of 1.9 and 2.1. It is tempting to declare the first model better, but the numbers are incomparable if tokenizers differ: one system may divide the same text into more prediction events. The dataset, normalization, token unit, and evaluation protocol define the quantity. Cross-entropy measures the code length assigned to observations under one stated distribution; it does not directly measure factuality, helpfulness, or usefulness in a downstream workflow.

Use the measure where it is strong. On a fixed corpus and tokenizer, loss exposes whether a model assigns more probability to held-out text. Then add the task-specific checks loss cannot express: evidence support, safety boundaries, cost, latency, and user success. An information measure is a precise instrument; it becomes misleading when asked to stand in for every product property.

Notebook: Check the quantity before trusting it

When comparing language-model losses, lock the corpus, tokenizer, normalization, and evaluation procedure. A lower number across different token units is not a direct capability comparison.

import numpy as np
x = np.array([2., -1.])
W = np.array([[1., 3.], [0., -2.]])
y = W @ x
print("shape", y.shape, "value", y)
# Write units and axis meanings beside every array.
What to test next. 1. Define distribution: Specify outcomes and conditioning context. 2. Score predictions: Compare assigned probability with observations. 3. Compress: Use predictable structure to reduce code length. 4. Interpret: Separate likelihood from usefulness and truth.

The gotcha. A small inspection script proves only the quantities it prints. Preserve units, shapes, versions, and the input fixture beside its output.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Define distribution. Specify outcomes and conditioning context.
  2. Score predictions. Compare assigned probability with observations.
  3. Compress. Use predictable structure to reduce code length.
  4. Interpret. Separate likelihood from usefulness and truth.

When comparing language-model losses, lock the corpus, tokenizer, normalization, and evaluation procedure. A lower number across different token units is not a direct capability comparison.

The gotcha. Passing each component check separately does not prove the composed path preserves identity, units, ordering, or authority.

Information measures depend on a distribution

Entropy measures expected uncertainty under one distribution. Cross-entropy measures the expected code length when observations follow one distribution and predictions use another. KL divergence measures their excess coding cost and is asymmetric.

  • Zero-probability assignments are catastrophic. An observed event given probability zero has infinite log loss, which is why numerical implementations clip or use stable logits.
  • Conditional entropy measures remaining uncertainty. Mutual information is the reduction in uncertainty about one variable after observing another.
  • Differential entropy is coordinate-dependent. Continuous entropy can be negative and does not behave like the discrete quantity under rescaling.
  • Tokenization changes the unit. Per-token language-model losses cannot be compared directly across different token vocabularies and segmentation rules.

The gotcha. Lower cross-entropy on fixed text measures predictive compression, not truth, reasoning, safety, or task value.

Compression connects prediction to representation

A predictor that assigns high probability to likely events can encode them with shorter descriptions. This link explains why next-token prediction learns structure, while also marking what the objective leaves unspecified.

  • Source coding exploits statistical regularity. The attainable average code length approaches entropy only under stated source assumptions and sufficiently capable codes.
  • Lossy compression defines a distortion measure. The rate-distortion tradeoff depends on which differences the metric treats as costly.
  • Bottlenecks can discard nuisance variation. Compression helps only when the discarded information is irrelevant to the downstream task.
  • Minimum description arguments include the model. A compact residual paired with an enormous decoder is not a compact explanation.

The gotcha. Calling a representation “compressed” is incomplete until the retained task, acceptable distortion, decoder, and total storage cost are stated.
